claims.text: importing INTO it resolves to a true edge, whereas a shell document's links are withheld from metrics either way, and links INTO it already resolve via ``known_all`` above, which is built from the record list rather than from the parse.
claims.why: The comment references 'shell document' and 'known_all' built from record list, but neither is defined in this chunk. The code shows doc_ignored skip but not shell handling.

claims.text: A SECOND pass over the same parse, deliberately. Reusing `targets` would mean building `document_links` from the wiki-aware superset, which silently moves an existing edge set -- the one thing this layer must not do. The cost is paid only when the flag is on.
claims.why: The claim about not reusing targets is a design rationale; the code shows a separate call to knowledge_links, but the claim about 'document_links' and 'existing edge set' cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: wiki_totals keys are documented in the codebase and must match the totals dict initialization.
claims.why: The wiki_totals dict is incremented but its initialization is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: ``kind`` is THE discriminator (markdown.DOCUMENT_KIND). The code-health keys are present and zero because zero is their true value for a file with no code -- keeping every existing joiner (report.py, score_modules, the web payload) working without a type switch -- and ``kind`` is what tells a reader those zeros describe an absence of code, not unhealthy code.
claims.why: The claim references external consumers (report.py, score_modules, web payload) not present in this chunk. The code sets kind and zeros as described.

claims.text: PLACED HERE ON PURPOSE, and the position is the review artifact: it is AFTER ``import_targets_by_rel`` is complete (the resolver FILTERS the import graph rather than recomputing imports, so a type edge can never contradict the import graph) and BEFORE ``_RESOLVER_CACHE`` is populated below -- so a reader can see with their eyes that ``build_resolver`` is called with ``all_units + doc_units`` and nothing type-shaped, which is invariant I2.
claims.why: The claim references '_RESOLVER_CACHE' and 'build_resolver' call with 'all_units + doc_units', none of which appear in this chunk. The code shows the type pass position relative to import_targets_by_rel completion, but invariant I2 cannot be verified.

claims.text: Nothing produced here is added to ``modules``, ``import_edges``, ``import_edges_reverse``, ``dep_edges``, ``fan_in``, ``all_units`` or ``lang_summary``; the three published keys are new keys.
claims.why: The code only assigns to type_blocks and does not modify any of the listed collections. The claim is consistent with the visible code.

claims.text: Reverse of ``import_targets_by_rel``: who imports ME. Built ONCE here because it is index-invariant, and ``semantic_slice`` is called in a loop against a single shared index (eval harness, web API) -- inverting the forward map inside the slicer would redo the same O(E) scan on every target.
claims.why: The claim references 'semantic_slice' and its usage, which is not present in this chunk. The code does build the reverse map as described.

observations.what: Document pass skips ignored rels, parses documents, collects links and wiki links if enabled, updates totals, and builds modules dict with zeros for code-health keys.
Type pass is conditional on types_on flag, calls resolve_type_graph with import_targets_by_rel and other arguments, and stores result in type_blocks.
Reverse import map import_sources_by_rel is built from import_targets_by_rel, and fan_in is initialized as defaultdict(int) from dep_edges values.
